title: Operate on recorded engineering work through reliable explicit commands
statement: Engineers and engineering agents need a reliable command-line interface for inspecting recorded work, recording explicitly chosen engineering decisions, and recovering interrupted updates without losing information or mistaking mechanical command success for engineering authority.

what.problem: Published command behavior, record preservation, and failure outcomes are not explicit in the initial REM model; broad knowledge and change capabilities alone do not explain how callers safely operate on the delivered recording interface.
what.desired_outcome: Callers can select useful recorded context, supply their own decisions, obtain faithful bounded outcomes, and recover interruption under the published command contract.

why.rationale: Automation and people depend on predictable commands, precise selection, preserved neighboring work, and outcomes that separate storage success from approval.

stakeholders: Engineers and reviewers operating on recorded engineering work
Engineering agents acting on explicit actor decisions
Maintainers and consumers of the published command-line interface

conditions: When selecting a command, inspecting project facts or exact recorded work, preparing or saving a decision, retrying or recovering an interrupted operation, and investigating an invocation.

contexts: The published local command-line interface and its supported registered change stores, explicit repository subjects, and private diagnostic state.

how.approach: Derive obligations from the current CLI and Record Format contracts while preserving their exact versions, public operations, closed vocabularies, limits, and preservation rules at their existing authoritative sources. Use black-box Scenarios and logical Functions to expose previously missing product capabilities.

how_much.scope: Covers current CLI command admission, discovery, selected reads, explicit recording, transaction recovery, result projection, and local diagnostics. Installation content and policy remain separately owned; only its generic command/result integration is included. This records current v3 workflow-store capabilities, not support for operating on the new REM design JSON, a replacement workflow decision engine, or a completed contract migration.

assumptions: Selected local storage and the existing execution environment are accessible; no new platform-support, hosting, disaster-recovery, or performance promise is introduced.
constraints: The CLI does not grant permission, choose workflow progression, or infer actor decisions from role labels, record shape, or command success.
Current docs/design/cli contracts remain authoritative for detailed behavior and independent version domains until explicitly reconciled by a controlled migration.

sources.basis: Recognizes the published command-line product need and mechanical safety obligations not fully expressed by the initial seven IRs; this is analytical representation, not runtime adoption of REM or approval transfer.
